title: Graded degradation SLOs for quantized variants and adaptive fallback routing
creator: Marisol Gomez
description: Motivation: As we expand support for quantized model variants and automatic fallback routing, teams need a clear, operational SLO matrix that describes latency targets, acceptable quality degradation bands, error budgets and automated rollout/rollback gates. This ticket defines per-step SLOs (full-precision -> 8-bit -> 4-bit -> smaller-model-fallback), acceptance criteria, monitoring signals and a staged canary plan that prioritizes availability while bounding user-visible quality regressions. The goal is to enable safe progressive rollouts of quantized variants for hosted API and Dedicated while providing deterministic rollback behavior when burn rates or quality regressions occur.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A published SLO matrix exists that enumerates P50/P95/P99 latency targets and a small set of fidelity metrics for each degradation step (full, 8-bit, 4-bit, fallback-model).

A2: Automated health checks and synthetic workload probes are defined and operational for short-gen (<=64 tokens) and long-gen (>=256 tokens) paths, running every 1m and reporting to the rollout dashboard.
A3: Canary rollout automation implements the staged progression: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated gating checks (error budget, fidelity delta, burn-rate).

A4: Rollback/mitigation rules are implemented: immediate rollback if error_budget_burn_rate > 5 for 10m OR quality_delta over evaluation set drops below threshold for 30m, and an operator-facing incident playbook is created and linked.
A5: Contract tests exercising token-level latency and fidelity thresholds pass in CI against the quantized variants and fallback routing logic with no flaky runs >2% in last 7 days.
A6: Dashboards for per-model SLO, per-tenant burn rate, and per-degradation-step fidelity score are live and accessible to Product, SRE and Solutions Engineering.
A7: Documentation (PRD + rollout runbook) is published with example configurations for Dedicated autoscaling policies that interact with graded degradation routing.
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in tail-latency P95 for the interactive chat workload by at least 20% when quantized variants are enabled under representative load, without increasing weekly error budget consumption by >10%.
SM2: At least 80% of tenant traffic eligible for quantized fallback shows fidelity_delta <= 0.06 (semantic similarity drop) measured by the in-house evaluation harness after rollout to 100%.
SM3: Zero Sev1 incidents attributed to incorrect routing or silent quality regressions during 30 days post-rollout for the first 10 enterprise customers enrolled in the program.
SM4: Automated canary gates successfully block progression at least once in staging tests during rollout rehearsals (validates gating logic).
slo_matrix_summary: Short-gen (<=64 tokens): full-precision P95 <= 180ms; 8-bit P95 <= 120ms; 4-bit P95 <= 90ms; fallback-model P95 <= 70ms. Long-gen (>=256 tokens) measured as steady-state token throughput: full-precision P50 token-ms <= 25ms; 8-bit P50 <= 18ms; 4-bit P50 <= 15ms. Availability SLO: 99.95% per-region per-month for interactive endpoints with graceful degradation lanes. Error budget allocation: 0.05% monthly error budget for catastrophic failures, per-degradation-step burn budgets proportioned 50/30/15/5 for full/8-bit/4-bit/fallback respectively.
monitoring_queries: P99 latency (per model): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="inference"}[5m])) by (le, model))
Per-step fidelity delta (semantic similarity): query_similarity_delta(eval_vector_baseline, eval_vector_variant) computed hourly
Error budget burn rate (per tenant): burn_rate = increase(errors_total[15m]) / increase(requests_total[15m]) compared against allocated error_budget
Synthetic canary check (short-gen): execute synthetic request set -> measure pass rate and mean similarity; fail if pass_rate < 98% or mean_similarity_drop > 0.06
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (staging): automated rehearsal with synthetic workload and canary gating. Stage 1 (canary 0.5%): run for 1h; allow progression only if burn_rate < 1.5 and fidelity_delta < configured threshold. Stage 2 (canary 5%): run for 6h with stricter checks (burn_rate < 1.2, fidelity checks hourly). Stage 3 (ramp 25%): run for 24h and validate per-tenant customer-facing quality metrics. Stage 4 (100%): gradual ramp remaining traffic over 48h with continuous monitoring. At each stage the orchestrator evaluates SLO health, per-tenant burn rates, and fidelity regressions; automated rollback triggers on sustained breach.
rollback_criteria: RC1: Sustained error budget burn rate > 4x for 10 continuous minutes at the canary scope.
RC2: Fidelity regression on golden-eval set: mean semantic-similarity drop > 0.08 sustained for 30 minutes.
RC3: User-facing increase in 4xx/5xx aggregated rate exceeding 0.02 of requests for 5 minutes.
RC4: Operator manually marks as blocked based on qualitative escalations from customer-reported incidents.
risks: R1: Semantic similarity thresholds may not fully capture user-perceived quality differences for some verticals (e.g., code generation).
R2: Per-tenant variance could cause safe global SLOs to miss tenant-specific regressions; need tenant-level gating and opt-out paths.
R3: Incorrect kernel selection or quantization artifacts could cause intermittent hallucinations not visible in standard evals.
R4: Overly aggressive fallback routing may increase downstream cost (duplicated requests) if not rate-limited.
out_of_scope: This ticket does not implement model quantization tooling or new quantization algorithms; those remain with Research/Infra (ENG). It also does not change pricing or billing behavior for quantized variants; finance product changes are separate.
notes: Design trade-offs: prioritize availability and latency improvements while bounding measurable fidelity loss; accept small controlled quality deltas for high-throughput tenants.
We will offer a per-tenant opt-out flag for quantized routing until confidence thresholds are met for each tenant.
Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to pilot with 3 willing customers before full 100% ramp.
